summary: Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA from the University of Oslo (attested 2008), where she studied under Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Liu Zaifu is a sinologist who studied at Xiamen University from around 1959 to 1963. He held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in 1963 and later at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1974), where he earned his Dr.phil.

Lobsang Gyatso specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959), he served as head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics from around 1973 to 1997.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jamspal studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1965–1972) and Columbia University under Alex Wayman (~1974–1991). He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia University.
Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Lobsang Shastri is a Tibetologist. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad Kumar Soni.

Tibetologist and historian Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD under Hildegard Diemberger at the University of Cambridge (-2014). He held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute and the University of Bonn.
Loden Sherab Dagyab is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, and held a post at the University of Bonn from approximately 1966 to 2004.

Lodrö Sangpo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra is an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied under Raghu Vira, at the University of the Punjab (~1943–1947), and Utrecht University (~1949–1950, PhD). He served as Secretary (~1955) and Director (~1963) of the IAIC.
Longlian was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under the traditional teacher Nenghai from around 1941 to 1967.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak worked in Tibetology and religious studies, studying under Sherab Tenzin Gyaltsen, Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and at Menri Monastery. He founded Triten Norbutse and Menri Monasteries, serving as Lopon at both institutions.

Lore Sander specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies, studying under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1962–1967). She held posts at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst (1987), Free University of Berlin (1994), Humboldt University, and LMU Munich.

Lori Meeks works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1999–2003) and others, completed a postdoc at Stanford (~2003–2004), and joined the University of Southern California as Assistant Professor (~2004).

Lorna Dewaraja was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at St Anne's College and served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Ceylon from around 1957 to 1978.

Lorne Ladner works in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (attested 2004) and served as an adjunct faculty member in the counseling program at Argosy University (attested 2004).

Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Princeton (~1967–1969) and Harvard (~1970–1972), held a post at Cambridge (~1992–1993), and served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2009).
